title: Orchestrated soft evacuation and ledger backfill consistency validation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create and validate an automated 'soft evacuation' procedure for passive regions that incrementally drains traffic using circuit-breaker heuristics, performs an idempotent ledger-style backfill of missed writes, and verifies ledger-to-kv consistency without large RTO/RPO regressions. Aim is to provide a repeatable, observable sequence that preserves SLOs and enables scheduled failover drills with minimal application disruption.
background: We currently have multiple active/passive recovery artifacts but lack a coordinated mechanism that 1) softly evacuates traffic from a degraded passive region, 2) replays or backfills write-ahead records in a ledger-consistent manner after promotion or restore, and 3) validates end-to-end SLO regression. Previous tickets focus on hard cutovers and snapshot restores; this work targets an incremental, canary-first approach to reduce risk and surface data divergence earlier.
approach: Design soft-evacuation flow: traffic fencing -> progressive circuit-breaker thresholds -> staged reroute to primary/alternate region
Implement ledger backfill engine: idempotent replay of write-ahead events with ordering guarantees and per-entity checksums
Introduce canary doorway: route 5% -> 25% -> 50% traffic buckets with automated SLO checks before each step
Integrate load-shedding TTL: shallow-dropping low-value requests (non-critical telemetry) to preserve tail latency
Add verification harness: itemized checksum diffs, sequence-number reconciliation, and differential query tests against read replicas
Automate drill orchestration: scheduler + playbook runner that executes the sequence and collects artifacts
runbook_steps: Stage 0 - Precheck: verify KV snapshot timestamps, healthy gossip mesh, and tokenstore writability
Stage 1 - Canary enable: flip canary circuit to divert 5% of traffic to target passive region and validate 1min SLO metrics
Stage 2 - Progressive drain: if canary passes, escalate to 25% then 50% with 5-10 minute observation windows
Stage 3 - Ledger capture: pause client writes in passive region, atomically mark ledger tail, and export incremental WAL segments
Stage 4 - Backfill replay: run idempotent replay to primary in replay-only mode with checksum verification per logical key
Stage 5 - Consistency audit: run differential queries (sampled and full-batch for hot keys) and produce reconciliation report
Stage 6 - Re-enable writes: once audit passes, re-enable normal routing and monitor for 30 minutes
Stage 7 - Postmortem and artifacts: store logs, diffs, and SLO time-series; run smoke tests and close drill ticket
validation_plan: Functional: unit/integration tests for ledger replay idempotency, ordering, and checksum validation
System: staged canary runs in staging environment with synthetic traffic shapes (burst, tail-heavy, long tails)
SLO: assert 99th percentile latency and error-rate do not regress beyond configured SLO guardrails during each escalation step
Data: automated reconciliation script must report <= 1 inconsistency per 10M operations for acceptance
Chaos: introduce transient packet loss and instance restarts during staging to validate robustness of backfill engine
success_criteria: Soft-evacuation procedure can move traffic from passive to active without manual intervention and obeys circuit-breaker thresholds
Ledger backfill completes with idempotent semantics and checksum parity across a 48-hour synthetic write workload
No SLO breach outside of the approved maintenance window during an end-to-end scheduled drill
Automated reconciliation report produced and stored in the run artifacts bucket
Playbook has clear rollback triggers and alerting hooks tied to console dashboards
rollback_plan: If any canary or escalation step fails SLO checks or the reconciliation report shows > 0.00001% inconsistency threshold, abort escalation, immediately revert routing (open circuit, re-enable previous route), and run targeted restore of WAL segments to the pre-evacuation marker. Notify on-call, create incident with tag 'soft-evac-failure' and capture forensic logs for a postmortem.
monitoring: Dashboard: SLO - latency (p50/p95/p99) per region, error rate, request volume
Alert: Canary SLO violation -> paging to on-call
Alert: Replay failure or checksum mismatch -> critical pager
Audit: reconciliation-report artifact stored with unique run id and linked in the ticket
Cost: backfill bytes and replay time tracked for billing and post-drill review
